answer: Make each identity expensive to mint: before an agent can earn, it posts a refundable bond that peers verify, and fraud slashes it to zero. A sudden comet-burst of newcomers stays harmless because every node costs its own stake, so forging a thousand sybils means locking a thousand bonds. Trust then grows slowly, like a cedar ring by ring or a sonnet line by line, never conjured overnight, making cheap mass identities economically pointless.
